finding.claim: maxAge is silently not enforced for tokens that lack an iat claim, so a token without iat stays valid until exp (or indefinitely if it has no exp) despite maxAge being configured.
finding.source: verify(token) with a token whose payload has no iat claim (e.g. issued by a signer with noTimestamp: true, signer.js:129).

trace.note: maxAge option adds an iat date validator
verifyToken skips any validator whose claim is absent: if (!(claim in payload)) continue
requiredClaims only enforces iat if the operator lists it explicitly
cacheSet maxAge bound is also conditional on typeof payload.iat === 'number'

finding.guards_checked: requiredClaims (verifier.js:301-307): only applies if operator lists iat. Cache bound (verifier.js:138): same conditional. index.d.ts:104 documents maxAge without requiring iat. No other check enforces iat presence when maxAge is set.

finding.claim: With the cache enabled, verify() throws a synchronous TypeError for Buffer tokens because the default cacheKeyBuilder calls token.split, which Buffer does not have.
finding.source: verify(token) where token is a Buffer; the type check at verifier.js:361 explicitly accepts Buffers.
finding.sink: cacheKeyBuilder(token) at verifier.js:372 (default hashToken), which calls token.split at utils.js:46.

trace.note: cache lookup runs when cache is enabled (createCache, verifier.js:94-97; off by default)
cache.get(cacheKeyBuilder(token)) with token still a Buffer
hashToken: token.split('.', 1) throws TypeError for Buffer

finding.guards_checked: Type check at verifier.js:361 accepts Buffer. No Buffer-to-string conversion before cacheKeyBuilder. decode() converts Buffers (decoder.js:14-15) but only after the cache lookup, so it never runs first. The throw happens before the callback or promise is created.

finding.claim: Signature segments are not checked for canonical base64url encoding, so one token has several distinct strings that all verify (non-zero unused trailing bits are ignored).
finding.source: verify(token) where the attacker alters the final character of the signature segment of a previously issued token.
finding.sink: verifySignature signature decoding at crypto.js:394 (Buffer.from(signature,'base64')) followed by the HMAC comparison at crypto.js:398.

trace.note: only the base64url alphabet is checked (BASE64URL_RE), not canonical trailing bits
validateAlgorithmAndSignature calls verifySignature with the raw segment
signature decoded with lenient Buffer base64 decoding
comment claims the signature is canonical by this point, which is not true

finding.guards_checked: Alphabet check (decoder.js:10,41-43). timingSafeEqual (crypto.js:398) compares decoded bytes, so it does not detect the non-canonical form. No length or canonical-form check exists.
